rundown: FireWolves beat Rush 12-11. FireWolves led 7-6 at the half and held on.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 27, 7:26 PM ET. It had Rush 66% and FireWolves 34%, projecting Rush 11.8 – FireWolves 9.8 (21.6 total, Rush by 2).

Final: Rush 11 – FireWolves 12. Wrong winner: it had Rush at 66%, and FireWolves (34%) won.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Rush came in with a 6% above average attack and a 7% stingier than average defense (0-0, 11.4 scored and 9.8 allowed a game over 18 games), worth about 25 and 25 games of evidence. Projected to score 11.8, they scored 11 (−0.8 goals, 7% under); projected to allow 9.8, they allowed 12 (+2.2 goals, 23% over).

FireWolves came in with a 6% below average attack and a 8% leakier than average defense (0-0, 9.9 scored and 11.8 allowed a game over 18 games), worth about 25 and 25 games of evidence. Projected to score 9.8, they scored 12 (+2.2 goals, 23% over); projected to allow 11.8, they allowed 11 (−0.8 goals, 7% under).

The bigger miss was FireWolves' scoring (+2.2 goals against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 23 against 21.6 projected (+1.4), about the 59th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±6).

Margin: FireWolves by 1 against Rush by 2 projected, about the 72nd percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±5).

An ordinary result: inside the range the simulations expected most of the time.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: inputs were missing (SAS lineup rating or past seasons, OSH lineup rating or past seasons); there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection landed within its normal range anyway, so the flags didn't cost it much this time.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×1.065 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +3 goals. It counts toward Lacrosse scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Lacrosse learning switches on at 20 graded games (1 so far).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total within its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
